messages:
Maya: Quick sync — proposing a gated rollout plan for 'routing-eviction-v2' (feature flag + canary + A/B). Need alignment on percentages, safety gates, and fallback behavior.

Leo: +1. High level: start 1% canary in us-west-2, monitor 15m windows, then 5% -> 20% -> 50% if healthy.

Anya: Define "healthy" concretely. My proposal: p95 latency <= baseline + 100ms, error rate < 0.5% absolute increase, and token cost delta < 15% (for same SLO). If any gate fails, auto-roll back to previous route.

Samir: For feature flags, we should use gradual ramp with tag-based gating: org tier (internal -> beta customers -> all). Flag keys: `routing-eviction-v2`, rollout_stage string: `internal|beta|public`.

Julia: From CS: include a opt-in beta cohort of 10 customers (manual assignment) to validate quality before public canary. Also notify those accounts via email.

Maya: Good call. So timeline: Internal 1% (internal infra) -> Beta 10 orgs (manual) -> Public 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%. Auto-scaling of dedicated pools allowed at public stages only.

Leo: Implementation notes: runtime will route by policy: prefer low-latency hosts, but `eviction-v2` can drop to `eviction-v1` variant when KV hit rate < 0.6. Fallback policy: when health-gates trip, route to `model-quant-small` in same region, then notify SRE.

Anya: Add emergency threshold: if error rate > 2% OR p95 > baseline + 500ms for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> immediate rollback and short-circuit requests to conservative route. Also automatic incident page created by DeployBot.

Samir: For A/B, we want an experiment to measure latency vs cost. A group gets `eviction-v2` + standard batching, B group gets `eviction-v1` + optimized batching. Metric: latency delta and cost per 1k tokens. Stat test: two-sided t-test after 100k requests.

Maya: Can we run A/B during the 5% -> 20% window? We'll need consistent hashing to avoid churn across requests.

Leo: Yes — use sticky user-based assignment via `user_id % 100` to assign A/B. Keep assignment stable for 24h.

QA-Bot: Preflight smoke: `canary-checks.sh` ran on internal pool, passed 8/10 (1 flaky reroute, 1 minor token delta). Full logs: https://internal.corp/reports/1815567890/canary.

Julia: Which issues are the flaky ones? I can escalate to owners.

QA-Bot: Flaky reroute occurred when KV load spiked -> fallback to v1. Repro steps in the log. Tagging @Leo.

Leo: I'll add a guard in the eviction path to throttle eviction work when kv_load > 0.8. Small patch, will submit PR today.

DeployBot: Scheduled canary rollout job created: job_id=rb-2026-03-20-01, start=1815600000 (UTC). Will post progress to #deploys.

Maya: Checklist before public canary: 1) PR merged for throttle guard (Leo), 2) Beta customers confirmed (Julia), 3) Monitoring dashboards with alert rules ready (Anya), 4) DeployBot job scheduled (done), 5) Rollback playbook updated in playbooks/canary-rollbacks.md.

Samir: Also add cost budget guard: if cost per 1k tokens for canary > projected by 25% for >30m -> pause rollout.

Anya: I'll add alert rules: `routing_eviction_v2_p95_increase`, `routing_eviction_v2_error_rate`, `routing_eviction_v2_cost_spike`. Alert severity: P0 for >2% errors, P1 for p95 breach, P2 for cost.

Maya: Sweet. I'll update the product spec and label launch criteria: all gates green for 24h in 50% window + green A/B stats. If green, move to 100% with a one-hour monitoring hold.

Julia: I'll reach out to beta customers today. List of 10 ready: Acme, NovaLabs, StreamLeap... sending invites.

Leo: Timeline looks good. PR ETA 3h, then canary creation.

Maya: Thanks all. If anyone hits blockers, drop notes here. Otherwise we'll reconvene at deploy start. :rocket:
